question.text:
For F(x, y) = (2x − y + 1, x + y), which statement is correct?
(A) There is a unique 2 × 2 matrix A with F (v) = Av for every v.
(B) No such 2 × 2 matrix exists, because F (0) ̸= 0.
(C) No such matrix exists, because the two components are different.
(D) Every 2 × 2 matrix with determinant three represents F .
(E) F is linear after merely reordering the ordinary basis vectors.

solution.text:
Any matrix product sends the zero vector to zero, but F (0, 0) = (1, 0). The nonzero trans-
lation prevents an ordinary matrix representation of the stated dimensions. Reordering a
basis changes coordinates, not the image of zero.
